stage_39_note: Opened by revisiting known gap #4 (full syllabic Chandas scansion unresolved). Wired in chandas_rulebook.json as a fifth directory Library file, used to ground -- not just cite -- a new computed IAST syllabification and guru/laghu classification mechanism (_syllabic_scansion), after verifying at runtime that the rulebook itself states the needed rules (chandas-2 varna definition, chandas-3 five-fold guru/laghu test, chandas-6 anushtubh structure). Two real bugs were caught and fixed empirically before delivery: (1) IAST aspirate digraphs (kh/gh/ch/jh/th/dh/ph/bh and retroflex equivalents) were being miscounted as 2 consonants instead of 1 in samyoga detection, causing false guru classifications -- fixed with a digraph-aware counter; (2) the Library-scansion cross-validation initially compared computed IAST text against the Library's Devanagari field as literal strings, always producing a false MISMATCH from script mismatch alone -- fixed by narrowing the cross-check to pada count only, with an honest note that no transliteration layer exists yet for a full text comparison. Result: 20/20 padas across all five verses now carry computed scansion; 19/20 match chandas-6's stated 6th/7th-syllable constraint exactly. The one exception, 1.1.1 pada 1, is a genuine computed mismatch, deliberately reported bare rather than explained via non-Library terminology (vipulā/pathyā etc. do not appear anywhere in chandas_rulebook.json, confirmed by direct search) -- flagged below for future correctness review. Evidence coverage unchanged at 87.27% -- Component 10 was already SOURCE_ASSERTION for every verse before this cycle; this adds computed depth the coarse component-slot metric doesn't register (see gap #9). Rulebook citation count unaffected (still 25) -- Component 10's grounding_citations are a separate, verse-scoped mechanism. Regression-tested in all three standard configurations (full / project-folder-only / fully degraded), confirming graceful None-return degradation when chandas_rulebook.json is unreachable.

stage_41_note: Opened from a 'which JSONs can we review now?' investigation: while diffing combined_shlokas_1-5_v81_regression_labels_sa.json against the already-integrated v8.1 file (found byte-identical for 4/5 verses, not independently worth integrating), re-examined the integrated v8.1 file's own full structure and found real, unused evidence sitting in COMPONENT_3_padavigraha.pada_vigraha -- a per-word meaning/etymology/morphology/role/POS/gender/number/case record, never once read by the engine for Component 3 despite this same file already being primary for Components 4/5/9/10. 47 of 64 word-occurrences across all 5 verses carry full content; the other 17 are honestly marked needs_review, the same pending-marker convention already used for Component 9/10. Verified 46 of those 47 join cleanly to a Component-1 word using only two documented formatting-only canonicalizations (hyphen-strip, trailing anusvara ं->म् normalization), codified as _c3_join_key. Wired _v81_padavigraha in and rebuilt _c3_padavigraha to consult it first, falling back to the existing Component-5 declension-table cell match only where the v8.1 file doesn't cover a word. Caught and fixed a real join-safety bug before delivery: the first implementation kept one Library entry per canonicalized key (flat dict), so a surface form repeated within a verse (कः x4 in 1.1.3, च x3 in 1.1.2) had every occurrence silently reuse the same single entry, including occurrences the Library file explicitly marked needs_review and did NOT vouch for -- fixed by making each key a queue, consumed one item per matching occurrence in the same left-to-right order Component 1's word list is walked. Verified against 1.1.3's item count by hand before and after the fix. Identified and verified, rather than bridged, a genuine textual-variant discrepancy: 1.1.4's Component-1 word 4 (द्युतिमान्, confirmed against sa_rAmAyaNa.txt R_1,001.004) has no v8.1 pada_vigraha match because the v8.1 entry at that position is keyed मतिमान् -- a different word (root मति vs root द्युति), not a formatting artifact; deliberately left unmatched and flagged below. Zero regressions programmatically verified: every previously-matched word stayed matched (with richer content), plus 10 newly-covered words including 1.1.3's विद्वान् (closing part of former gap #3). Regression-tested in all three standard configurations, 5/5 PASS in each. Evidence coverage unchanged at 87.27% -- Component 3 was already populated for every verse except the still-open 1.1.3/1.1.5 samasa-adjacent gaps; this replaces thin/partial per-word content with real Library evidence underneath already-supported slots (see gap #9).
